name: Cologne Cathedral
scaleNote: 0.35 studs per metre. At 0.6 the two spires alone were most of 36 960 placements; the site's whole claim is that 157 m of tower stands over 144 m of church, and that reads at any scale where both are on screen.

spireHeight.source: Wikipedia, Cologne Cathedral: 'At 157 m (515 ft), the cathedral is the tallest twin-spired church in the world'.

length.source: Wikipedia, Cologne Cathedral: 'External length | 144.58 m (474.3 ft)'.

width.source: Wikipedia, Cologne Cathedral: 'External width | 86.25 m (283.0 ft)'.

note:
Three cited numbers and nothing else: no source read here gives the nave height or the transept width, so the body of the church is a block of the cited length and width at an uncited height, and the two spires are `Column`s of the cited height. That is a thin model of a very elaborate building, and the elaboration is the part a Klemmbaustein cannot do anyway.

ACTIVE PLACE OF WORSHIP. Included under Stefan's 'build all of them', not decided individually.

The two spires stand WEST of the nave and the transept is two arms either side of it, not one block through it. Both were overlaps: a transept crosses a nave in a real church and shares its volume, which is exactly what the brick grid forbids.
